keyVerseText: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
rootMeaning: The word ἐκπλήρωσις (ekplḗrōsis) derives from the verb ἐκπληρόω (ekplēróō), meaning 'to fulfill' or 'to accomplish entirely.' This root conveys the idea of something being completed or brought to its full measure from start to finish. Unlike the general English term 'completion,' the Greek root emphasizes the thorough fulfillment or the carrying out of a purpose to its intended end.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἐκπλήρωσις appears only once, specifically in Acts 21:26, where it is translated as 'the accomplishment.' This singular occurrence highlights its meaning as the fulfillment or completion of a divinely appointed period or requirement. The consistent translation as 'accomplishment' underscores its use to denote the precise carrying out or completion of a prescribed action or time.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐκπλήρωσις enriches our grasp of God's sovereign plan as one that is perfectly fulfilled and completed according to His purposes. It reminds believers that divine promises and ordinances are not partial or incomplete but are accomplished fully in God's timing. This term points to the faithfulness of God in bringing His redemptive work to its intended conclusion, encouraging trust in His perfect fulfillment of all things in Christ. The concept of fulfillment also invites believers to live in the assurance that what God has set in motion will reach its consummation.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 21:26 speaks of Paul purifying himself to signify 'the accomplishment of the days of purification,' indicating that a divinely appointed period was being brought to its full and proper end. The use of ἐκπλήρωσις here highlights that this was not merely a ritual act but the completion of a significant phase in God's redemptive timeline. This word deepens our understanding of the verse by emphasizing that the purification days were fulfilled entirely, pointing to the faithfulness of God's covenantal processes.
